canonical_name: Whitaker's Words -- a Latin morphological analyser and dictionary in Ada (Col. William Whitaker, 1993-2006; maintained by Martin Keegan)
lineage: A large REAL Ada program (tens of thousands of lines) from the language's first generation: parses Latin word forms into stem + inflection against a 39,000-entry dictionary, handling enclitics, tackons, prefixes/suffixes and syncope; runs on DOS/Windows/Unix for three decades. Public domain by its author. The Ada culture's strong typing and packages are visible throughout.
version: github.com/mk270/whitakers-words master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

license.status: public domain (author's statement); see LICENSE in the tree

entry_points: bin/words <latin word> ; the dictionary build (makedict/makestem/makeinfl) produces DICTFILE.GEN etc.

example.output: its parse: amo, amare, amavi, amatus V (1st) ... 'love'

upstream_docs: Whitaker, WORDS documentation (doc/ in the tree)

human_capability_summary.built_to: explain any Latin word form by finding which stem plus which inflection could produce it, against a real dictionary
human_capability_summary.pressure: morphological ambiguity, a large dictionary, DOS-era memory limits the design still shows
human_capability_summary.success_means: known forms parse to the right lemma and inflection; unknown forms are reported as such

human_environmental_pressure: ambiguity, dictionary scale, limited memory (1990s PCs)
human_failure_condition: a form is parsed to a wrong lemma or missed
behavioral_entry_point: feed rare, syncopated or enclitic forms (amavisse, amaveruntque) and inspect the analysis trace

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run whitakers-words-ada
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: explain any Latin word form by finding which stem plus which inflection could produce it, against a real dictionary
